articles.title: The United States initiates anti-dumping and countervailing duty investigations into certain amine compounds from China, with the maximum tariff reaching 352.32%. - ChemNet News
articles.summary: The United States initiates anti-dumping and countervailing duty investigations into certain amine compounds from China, with the maximum tariff reaching 352.32%.  ChemNet News
articles.full_text:
The United States initiates anti-dumping and countervailing duty investigations into certain amine compounds from China, with the maximum tariff reaching 352.32%.
On October 20, 2026, Eastern Time, the U.S. Department of Commerce officially announced the launch of anti-dumping (AD) and countervailing duty (CVD) investigations into certain amine compounds originating from China.
The investigation was initiated by U.S. enterprises Evonik Corporation and Huntsman International LLC. Once the final ruling is issued, relevant Chinese exporting enterprises will face high tariffs ranging from 97.71% to 352.32%, and China's polyurethane catalyst industry will face obvious pressure on exports to the U.S.
The U.S. alleges that the dumping margin of the involved Chinese products ranges from 244.94% to 352.32%; it also determines that the subsidy rate of the involved products exceeds the de minimis standard (2%), meeting the conditions for initiating a countervailing duty investigation.
Screenshot of the U.S. Department of Commerce Announcement
According to U.S. Customs statistics, the U.S. imported approximately $375 million worth of such amine compounds from China in 2024, and the import value dropped to $235 million in 2025; Chinese products hold a 30% market share in the U.S. and are one of the core sources of such products for the U.S.
Definition of Involved Products and Downstream Applications
The investigation targets amine catalysts used in the reaction of isocyanates with hydroxyl-containing substances such as polyols and water, which are core auxiliaries in polyurethane systems and widely used in flexible polyurethane foam, rigid foam, coatings, adhesives, elastomers, and other fields.
The corresponding HTSUS tariff numbers for the involved products mainly include: 2909.11.00.00, 2922.19.96.90, 2921.29.00.55, 2934.99.90.01, and may also fall under subheadings 2921.21.00.00 and 3815.90.50.00.
Downstream Subdivided Application Fields
1. Flexible Polyurethane Foam: Furniture sponges, mattresses, car seats, headrests, etc., are the largest application segment of the catalysts involved in this investigation;
2. Rigid Polyurethane Foam: Building insulation spray foam, refrigerator/freezer insulation layers, pipeline insulation materials;
3. Other Systems: Polyurethane coatings, adhesives, sealants, elastomers, etc.
There is a key rule of origin in this investigation: For goods processed in a third country through mixing, dilution, component adjustment, etc., if the materials contain amine compounds originating from China, such amine compounds shall still be deemed as originating from China, and it is impossible to avoid this dual investigation through simple overseas processing.
Overview of Major Domestic Manufacturers and Production Capacity
The involved amine compounds are essentially tertiary amine catalysts for polyurethane. Domestic manufacturers are concentrated in the polyurethane auxiliary sector, with leading enterprises supporting the entire industrial chain and small and medium-sized manufacturers focusing on specialty amines:
1. Wanhua Chemical is the leader in China's polyurethane catalyst industry. Relying on the MDI entire industrial chain synergy, its core products include N,N-dimethylcyclohexylamine (DMCHA), pentamethyldiethylenetriamine (PMDETA), etc., covering all scenarios of tertiary amine catalysts for flexible foam and rigid foam. Its total production capacity of tertiary amine catalysts is 68,000 tons per year, with a leading domestic market share. It also supports its own downstream polyurethane demand and is an important enterprise for exports to the U.S.
2. Jiangsu Meiside is a professional leader in polyurethane auxiliaries, with two production bases in Nanjing and Jilin. Its production capacity of organic amine catalysts is 25,000 tons per year, supporting silicone foam stabilizers. Its products cover furniture flexible foam, home appliance rigid foam, and other fields, and are widely supplied to domestic and overseas polyurethane compound material manufacturers.
3. Jiangsu Yake Technology is a high-end tertiary amine catalyst manufacturer, specializing in high-purity specialty amines, with outstanding advantages in building insulation and refrigerator rigid foam. Its production capacity of tertiary amine catalysts is 49,000 tons per year, and it can provide customized catalyst formula products.
4. Zhejiang Huangma Technology is an integrated enterprise of surfactants and polyurethane auxiliaries, with a production capacity of 36,000 tons per year for tertiary amine catalysts. It has long-term supporting cooperation with home appliance insulation material enterprises, and its rigid foam catalysts are stably delivered in the market.
5. Anhui Hengguang is a specialty amine catalyst enterprise for polyurethane materials (Hengguang New Materials). Its existing amine catalyst production capacity is 3,000 tons per year; after all the under-construction specialty amine projects are put into operation, the total production capacity of specialty amines can reach 20,000 tons per year, focusing on low-odor, high-performance polyurethane amine catalysts.
6. Liyang Jiangdian Chemical has been deeply engaged in polyurethane catalysts for many years, with a total production capacity of 1,200 tons per year for various polyurethane amine catalysts. Its products cover subdivided categories such as flexible foam, high-resilience foam, and melamine catalysis.
Brief Analysis of Industry Impact
This dual investigation targets core polyurethane catalysts, not end foam products. If the final high tariffs are imposed, the export competitiveness of relevant domestic enterprises directly exporting to the U.S. will be greatly weakened.
On the one hand, domestic manufacturers may accelerate their response to the investigation and adjust their export strategies; on the other hand, downstream furniture, automobile, and insulation material enterprises in the U.S. will face rising raw material costs. U.S.-based Huntsman and Evonik, as the applicants of this investigation, will directly benefit from the import tariff barriers.
Industry insiders remind that domestic exporting enterprises should sort out their product tariff numbers and origin determinations as soon as possible, evaluate the feasibility of responding to the investigation, and at the same time develop non-U.S. markets such as Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and Latin America to reduce their dependence on the single U.S. market.
Subsequently, the U.S. International Trade Commission (USITC) will make a preliminary ruling on industry injury within 45 days, and then a series of procedures such as the preliminary and final rulings of the Department of Commerce will be carried out in sequence.

Disclosure
Commerce intends to disclose the calculations and analysis performed in connection with the final results of this administrative review to interested parties within five days of any public announcement or, if there is no public announcement, within five days of the publication date of this notice in accordance with 19 CFR 351.224(b).
Assessment Rate
Pursuant to section 751(a)(2)(C) of the Act, and 19 CFR 351.212(b)(1), Commerce will determine, and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) shall assess, antidumping duties on all appropriate entries covered by this review. Pursuant to 19 CFR 351.212(b)(1), for Suncity, we calculated importer-specific antidumping duty assessment rates by aggregating the total amount of dumping calculated for the examined sales of each importer and dividing each of these amounts by the total entered value associated with those sales. Where we did not have entered values for all U.S. sales to a particular importer, we calculated an importer-specific, per-unit assessment rate on the basis of the ratio of the total amount of dumping calculated for the importer's examined sales to the total quantity of those sales.[5]
To determine whether an importer-specific, per-unit assessment rate is
de minimis,
in accordance with 19 CFR 351.106(c)(2), we also calculated an importer-specific
ad valorem
ratio based on estimated entered values. Where either the respondent's weighted-average dumping margin is zero or
de minimis
within the meaning of 19 CFR 351.106(c)(1), or an importer specific assessment rate is zero or
de minimis,
we will instruct CBP to liquidate the appropriate entries without regard to antidumping duties.
Commerce's “automatic assessment” will apply to entries of subject merchandise during the POR produced by Suncity for which the company did not know that the merchandise it sold to an intermediary (
e.g.,
a reseller, trading company, or exporter) was destined for the United States. In such instances, we will instruct CBP to liquidate such entries at the all-others rate established in the less-than-fair-value investigation if there is no rate for the intermediate company(ies) involved in the transaction.[6]
Commerce intends to issue assessment instructions to CBP no earlier than 35 days after the date of publication of the final results of this review in the
Federal Register
. If a timely summons is filed at the U.S. Court of International Trade, the assessment instructions will direct CBP not to liquidate relevant entries until the time for parties to file a request for a statutory injunction has expired (
i.e.,
within 90 days of publication).

The investment follows Paramount’s recent $111bn merger with Warner Bros Discovery, a huge acquisition that brought the media companies together under the Skydance name. At the head of the new media empire is David Ellison, the son of billionaire Oracle co-founder and Donald Trump ally Larry Ellison.
The Guardian has contacted Musk and Skydance for comment.
The cash infusion solidifies an alliance between two of Trump’s richest monetary backers. In September, Semafor reported that Paramount executives had considered Musk as an equity investor, citing his close ties to Larry Ellison, who invested $1bn in Musk’s acquisition of X in 2022 and also $45m in support of Trump’s re-election bid in 2024. Musk spent more than $290m on Trump’s re-election bid and has spent more than $350m backing Republicans in the current US midterm elections.
After the merger, Skydance co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz, who previously led Mattel, informed employees that the integration would involve layoffs, stating: “Integrating two companies will bring change, including difficult decisions that affect our workforce.”
The company’s leadership – which now oversees Paramount and Warner Bros’s movie studios, HBO Max, CBS News and CNN – has set a target of more than $6bn in cost savings over the next three years, a goal that Los Angeles county officials estimate could lead to the loss of 4,500 film and television jobs in Los Angeles alone.
Prior to the merger, a coalition of 12 states, including California and New York, sued Paramount, arguing that the deal would “extinguish” competition and result in “higher prices, lower quality and less content for film and television”.
In September, a settlement agreement required Skydance to release at least 30 films and more than 180 television shows annually, while ensuring that CBS and CNN maintain editorial independence.

articles.title: Meta strikes deal with Mark Zuckerberg to help him foot billionaire tax bill
articles.summary: Chief executive agrees to remain in California for eight years even if state brings in one-off 5% wealth taxMeta has struck a deal with Mark Zuckerberg to help him foot a possible California wealth tax targeting billionaires.The social media company behind Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp revealed on Wednesday night that the arrangement would keep its chief executive living in California, where Meta’s headquarters are located. Continue reading...
articles.full_text:
Meta has struck a deal with Mark Zuckerberg to help him foot a possible California wealth tax targeting billionaires.
The social media company behind Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp revealed on Wednesday night that the arrangement would keep its chief executive living in California, where Meta’s headquarters are located.
Under the deal, Zuckerberg will receive new shares that could be sold to potentially foot a multibillion-dollar tax bill in the event that California passes a one-off billionaire tax. In return, he is committed to remain a resident of the state, or wherever Meta maintains its base, for eight years.
Californians will vote early next month on Proposition 40, a one-off 5% tax on the roughly 250 billionaires who live in the state.
Zuckerberg, worth $239bn (£180bn) according to Forbes, told Meta he was considering moving his primary residence elsewhere because Prop 40 could expose him to a massive tax liability, potentially forcing him to sell voting shares to pay it.
In response, Meta is creating a new class of non-voting shares via a two-for-one stock split for all existing shareholders. This will allow Zuckerberg to sell some of these new class C shares to pay a potential tax bill, without diluting his control of the company.
Recent polling has shown that Prop 40 remains short of majority support with voters. Tech billionaires have been spending heavily to fight the measure, including the Google co-founder Sergey Brin, the Palantir co-founder Peter Thiel and the former Google CEO Eric Schmidt.
Rohit Khanna, the US congressman representing California’s 17th congressional district, has described Prop 40 as a choice between standing with the working class or the oligarchs.
“Every society is taxed. The only question is who will pay,” Khanna wrote in the Guardian last week.
“In Trump’s America, working people pay more than they should, while billionaires are so unburdened that they are becoming trillionaires. In the America we seek, billionaires and trillionaires will pay their fair share, while working people will be unburdened.”
Meta also reported a 26% rise in revenues for the last quarter to $64.6bn, beating expectations of $63.3bn. But profits fell by 37% to $13bn, dragged down by a $9.9bn charge related to Meta’s lawsuit over child protection and social media addiction failings.
The company’s shares slid by more than 6% when trading opened on Wall Street on Thursday, helping to drag the tech-focused Nasdaq index down 2.5% amid a wider selloff of AI-linked stocks.
In a separate case, on Wednesday a judge in New Mexico ordered Meta to pay $25bn following a trial that found the company had misled the public about how it handled Facebook user data.
Meta also revealed that it had cut its headcount to 66,775 at the end of September, 15% fewer than a year ago.
Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title: Barclays to cut 5,000 jobs as bank’s bosses hail AI productivity advances
articles.summary: Equating to the loss of 5% of its 93,000 global staff, job cuts come as bank announces jump in quarterly profitsBarclays is cutting 5,000 jobs as part of wider cost-saving plans that its bosses say are being driven by advances in AI.The job cuts will mean losing about 5% of the bank’s 93,000 global staff, with executives confirming they had already cut 1,000 workers since the start of the year. articles.full_text:
Barclays is cutting 5,000 jobs as part of wider cost-saving plans that its bosses say are being driven by advances in AI.
The job cuts will mean losing about 5% of the bank’s 93,000 global staff, with executives confirming they had already cut 1,000 workers since the start of the year.
The bank’s chief financial officer, Anna Cross, told reporters on Thursday that the job cuts were part of plans to save more than £1.1bn in 2027. “These actions involve an expected reduction of circa 5,000 full-time employees. Around 60% of the group actions relate to support functions, including fewer developers, as AI makes our people more productive.”
When asked how many of the total job cuts would be directly linked to advances in AI, the chief executive, CS Venkatakrishnan, said the bank had been making “deep investments” in technology and simplifying its processes.
“That is driving the bulk of the efficiency gains that you’ve seen so far. AI has an important role to play and may have a more important role to play in the future,” Venkatakrishnan said, calling AI the “icing on the cake” to modernising the bank’s technology.
Sharon Graham, the general secretary of the Unite union, said Barclays workers “deserve better”.
 
She added: “The company is using AI as an excuse to discard its loyal and long-suffering workforce. Employers should be focused on upgrading employees’ skills so that they remain employed as new technology changes the workplace. Instead, Barclays is guilty of taking a short-term, kneejerk approach.”
The news comes months after another UK-headquartered bank, Standard Chartered, announced plans to cut more than 7,000 jobs in the next four years as it ramps up the use of AI. It will mean slashing about 15% of its back-office roles by 2030.
Barclays also announced plans to hand a further £500m to investors, taking the total amount given to shareholders since January – through buybacks and dividends – to £2.8bn.
It came as the lender reported £2.3bn in pre-tax profits over the July to September quarter, up 12% from £2.1bn during the same period last year.
The strong financial performance will probably to be used to justify the expected increase in bank taxes in the 28 October budget, as Andy Burnham’s government looks for ways to raise revenue to help fund cost of living support programmes.
When asked whether the bank might consider tilting assets or investment out of the UK and to the US – where it also has operations – as a result of higher levies, Venkatakrishnan said Barclays would be able to absorb them.
“I recognise that the chancellor and the government … have to balance a host of considerations,” he said, adding that Barclays shared their goal to prompt growth.
“This is not a question of a financial hit to us. It’s bearable. It is a question of proportion and it’s a question of market signalling. But … I deeply respect the responsibility that the chancellor has and he has our full support and backing.”
Barclays’ strong performance included a 6% rise in net interest income at its UK retail banking operations, to £2bn. The figure has become a flashpoint for campaigners pushing for a bank tax.
It accounts for how much money banks make from loan charges, minus what they pay on deposits, and is linked to interest rates, which have been rising as the Iran war has driven up inflation expectations.
The Trades Union Congress, which has been campaigning for a bank tax increase, said lenders needed to contribute more at a time when people were struggling with household bills.
The TUC general secretary, Paul Nowak, said: “Barclays’ bumper profits aren’t an anomaly. All the big banks are doing exceptionally well … Britain’s big four banks have made £200bn in profit since 2021. They can – and should – pay more tax.”
Healey has promised that next week’s budget will support Britain’s entrepreneurs, and focus on cutting the “cost of business”.
He told the Times: “I want to be a chancellor who backs business in Britain making a profit, those entrepreneurs who in the end are the ones who challenge the status quo, come up with innovative ideas and are trying, some of them through sheer bloody-mindedness, to keep going through these sorts of pressures, which is what they’ve done.”

articles.title: French borrowing costs overtake US amid budget turmoil
articles.summary: France’s bond market hit by another bout of selling as country recovers from weekend protestsFrench borrowing costs continued to rise on Thursday, as investors fret that France’s government is struggling to pass a federal budget after public protests gripped the country.France’s bond market was hit with another bout of selling, with the difference between French and German 10-year borrowing costs – a metric for the risk premium attached to French debt – rising to its highest level in almost 15 y...
articles.full_text:
French borrowing costs continued to rise on Thursday, as investors fret that France’s government is struggling to pass a federal budget after public protests gripped the country.
France’s bond market was hit with another bout of selling, with the difference between French and German 10-year borrowing costs – a metric for the risk premium attached to French debt – rising to its highest level in almost 15 years.
The yield on the French 10-year bond – known as obligation assimilables du Trésor (Oat) – rose by nine basis points to 5.089% in early trading on Thursday, its highest level since July 2022. It broke across the 5% threshold on Wednesday for the first time since 2002.
The move lifted France’s 10-year borrowing costs over the equivalent for US Treasury bonds for the first time since 2013.
The volatility comes as the French government struggles to pass a budget for next year, while the country recovers from widespread protests that turned violent last weekend.
Tens of thousands of people had attended peaceful marches to demand more teachers and repairs to decrepit schools, but different groups clashed with police in cities including Paris, Bordeaux, Nice and Marseille in recent days.
Public buildings were attacked, and thousands of shops and businesses were looted. The interior ministry said there had been nearly 2,400 arrests.
Meanwhile, a parliamentary gridlock has blocked plans by the president, Emmanuel Macron, to increase the state pension age from 62 to 64 and a series of measures designed to rein in state spending.
France’s budget deficit was 5.1% of gross domestic product in 2025, while its debt pile stood at 115.6% of GDP.
It comes as the country also grapples with higher inflation triggered by the war in Iran, with many governments with big debt piles coming under acute pressure.
Jim Reid, a market strategist at Deutsche Bank, said the sell-off in French government bonds was starting to ripple out to other countries, too.
“Among others, the Italian 10-year spread over [German bonds] widened 3.8 basis points to 116 basis points, while Spain’s widened 3.1 basis points to 66 basis points, marking its widest level since June 2025,” he said.
Carsten Brzeski of the bank ING said rising yields had reinforced the European Central Bank’s “restrictive” monetary policy stance before its interest rate decision next week. The bank last raised its key interest rate to 2.5% in September.
“The ECB is very likely to stay on hold next week and will delay any next rate hike decision to December,” he said.
“Any solution to the current French fiscal woes could bring some relief to bond markets and allow the ECB to continue hiking rates. Without any solution, bond markets have taken over the ECB’s role, making rate hikes less likely.”

AGENCY:

ACTION:
Notice of Information Collection, request for comment.
SUMMARY:
The Department of Commerce, in accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) of 1995, invites the general public and other Federal agencies to comment on proposed, and continuing information collections, which helps us assess the impact of our information collection requirements and minimize the public's reporting burden. The purpose of this notice is to allow for 60 days of public comment on the proposed revision to the Annual Business Survey prior to the submission of this information collection request (ICR) to OMB for approval.
DATES:
To ensure consideration, comments regarding this proposed information collection must be received on or before December 21, 2026.
ADDRESSES:
Interested persons are invited to submit written comments by email to
Matthew.J.Tucker@census.gov.
Please reference Annual Business Survey in the subject line of your comments. You may also submit comments, identified by Docket Number USBC-2026-0562 to the Federal e-Rulemaking Portal:
http://www.regulations.gov.
All comments received are part of the public record. No comments will be posted to
http://www.regulations.gov
for public viewing until after the comment period has closed. Comments will generally be posted without change. All Personally Identifiable Information (for example, name and address) voluntarily submitted by the commenter may be publicly accessible. Do not submit Confidential Business Information or otherwise sensitive or protected information. You may submit attachments to electronic comments in Microsoft Word, Excel, or Adobe PDF file formats.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Requests for additional information or specific questions related to collection activities should be directed to Patrice Hall, Assistant Division Chief, R&D and Special Surveys, 301-763-7198,
patrice.n.hall@census.gov.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
I. Abstract
In an effort to improve the measurement of business dynamics in the United States, the Census Bureau is conducting the Annual Business Survey (ABS). The ABS combines Census Bureau firm-level collections to reduce respondent burden, increase data quality, reduce operational costs, and operate more efficiently. The ABS measures research and development (R&D), innovation, business owner characteristics, and other topics of interest. The ABS is a joint statistical project between the Census Bureau and the National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics (NCSES) within the U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF).
The 2026 ABS (collected during 2027) will remove the following business owner demographic questions:
Race
Ethnicity
Sex
Place of Birth
U.S. Citizenship, and
Age
Estimates for this data will be produced through use of various administrative data. The Census Bureau, in collaboration with NCSES, plans to research additional administrative and survey data sources to replace the other owner characteristics questions on the survey in future survey cycles. While this research continues, select business owner characteristics questions (
e.g.,
disability, education level) will remain
( printed page 66670)
on the survey. The Business Enterprise Research and Development survey (BERD), which merged with the ABS beginning with reference year 2025, will continue to be included within the ABS.
The ABS will sample 230,000 businesses and nonprofit organizations (222,000 employer business; 8,000 nonprofit organizations). The ABS includes all nonfarm employer businesses filing Internal Revenue Service (IRS) tax forms as individual proprietorships, partnerships, or any other type of corporation, with non-zero receipts or payroll. Also included are nonprofit organizations to measure their research activities. The ABS samples approximately 8,000 nonprofit organizations who are required to complete IRS form 990. The nonprofit sample will yield national estimates of R&D performance within the nonprofit sector. Of note, nonprofit organizations will only see questions relating to research activities and will not be asked any questions relating to owner demographics.
The ABS is designed to incorporate new content, on a rotating basis, each survey year based on topics of relevance. Each year new questions are submitted to the OMB for approval.
The 2026-2028 ABS will collect the following information from employer businesses:
Company information including sales, employees, and business ownership from all employer businesses.
Select business owner characteristics questions (e.g.,
disability, education level) from the principal owner(s) of the business.
Business characteristics from all employer businesses.
Research, development, and related topics from select businesses and nonprofits.
Innovation data and data on critical and emerging technologies from all employer businesses.
Management practices and employee training data from all employer businesses.
Intellectual property protection and technology transfer data from all employer businesses.
Other potential module topics such as cybersecurity and financing.
II. Method of Collection
The ABS utilizes an online survey instrument. Respondents are mailed and emailed letters directing them to create a Census account and access the survey through their account. The online survey automatically skips questions that do not apply and checks for common errors. Detailed question instructions will be embedded in the electronic instrument where appropriate. Responses will be due approximately 30 days from initial mailing.

Reliant, a Delaware limited liability company headquartered in Hastings, Minn., seeks Board authority to acquire control of the Additional Carriers by purchasing 100% of the equity interests from Sellers. (Appl. 2, 21.) [1]
According to the application, Reliant is a noncarrier company that was formed to own, operate, and manage various motor carriers of passengers and related companies. (
Id.
at 2.) Applicants state that Reliant does not itself conduct regulated motor carrier operations and that it is owned and controlled, through a series of noncarrier holding companies, by several investment entities associated with Tiger Infrastructure Partners LP (Tiger Infrastructure). (
Id.
) [2]
The application states that at the top of the ownership chain is Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund IV AIV LP,[3]
which owns 100% of TIP MN Investments LP,[4]
which in turn owns 100% of TIP MNC Acquisition, LLC (collectively, Tiger Infrastructure Investment Entities).[5]
(Appl. 2-3.) TIP MNC Acquisition, LLC owns 73.56% of MNC Holdings, LP, which owns 100% of MNC Intermediate Holdings, LLC, which owns 100% of MNC Parent, LLC, which in turn owns 100% of Reliant. (Appl. 3.)
According to the application, Reliant's upstream ownership forms part of a broader transportation investment platform affiliated with Tiger Infrastructure, a private equity
( printed page 66770)
infrastructure investment firm founded in 2010 that is focused on growth equity investments across transportation, digital infrastructure, and energy transition sectors in North America and Europe. (
Id.
at 3.) In January 2025, the Board approved Tiger Infrastructure's indirect acquisition of control of seven interstate motor carriers of passengers through the Tiger Infrastructure Investment Entities and through the following intermediate holding companies: MNC Holdings, LP; MNC Intermediate Holdings, LLC; MNC Parent, LLC; and MNC Transportation, LLC (then referred to as Minnesota Borrower, LLC). (

See TIP Minn. Coaches Acquis. LLC—Acquis. of Control—Marschall Line, Inc.,
MCF 21127 (STB served Jan. 8, 2025). Id.)
Applicants state that as a result of that post-closing reorganization and a subsequent acquisition of control transaction earlier this year,[6]
Reliant is an indirect owner of nine federally regulated interstate motor carriers of passengers (collectively, Affiliated Carriers). (
Id.
at 4.) The Affiliated Carriers are:

While Marschall Line occasionally conducts charter trips that cross state lines into Wisconsin or other neighboring states, these interstate movements are incidental and limited when compared to the company's predominantly intrastate operations within Minnesota. AGENCY:
Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
ACTION:
Draft report; request for comment.
SUMMARY:
The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is issuing for public comment a draft report entitled, NUREG-1307, Revision 21, “Report on Waste Burial Charges: Changes in Decommissioning Waste Disposal Costs at Low-Level Waste Burial Facilities.” This report, which is revised periodically, explains the formula acceptable to the NRC for determining the minimum decommissioning fund requirements for nuclear power reactor licensees, as required by NRC regulations. Specifically, this report provides the adjustment factor and updates the values for the labor, energy, and waste burial escalation factors of the minimum formula.
DATES:
Submit comments by November 23, 2026. Comments received after this date will be considered if it is practical to do so, but the Commission is able to ensure consideration only for comments received before this date.
ADDRESSES:
You may submit comments by any of the following methods; however, the NRC encourages electronic comment submission through the Federal rulemaking website:
Federal rulemaking website:
Go to

and search for Docket ID NRC-2026-4588. Address questions about Docket IDs in

Emil Tabakov, Office of Nuclear Material Safety and Safeguards, U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, Washington, DC 20555-0001; telephone: 301-415-6814; email:
Emil.Tabakov@nrc.gov.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
I. Obtaining Information and Submitting Comments
A. Obtaining Information
Please refer to Docket ID NRC-2026-4588 when contacting the NRC about the availability of information for this action. You may obtain publicly available information related to this action by any of the following methods:
NRC's Agencywide Documents Access and Management System (ADAMS):
You may obtain publicly available documents online in the ADAMS Public Documents collection at
https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/adams.html.
To begin the search, select “Begin ADAMS Public Search.” For problems with ADAMS, please contact the NRC's Public Document Room (PDR) reference staff at 1-800-397-4209, at 301-415-4737, or by email to
PDR.Resource@nrc.gov.
Draft NUREG-1307, Revision 21, “Report on Waste Burial Charges: Changes in Decommissioning Waste Disposal Costs
( printed page 66743)
at Low-Level Waste Burial Facilities,” is available in ADAMS under Accession No. ML26271A165.
NRC's PDR:
The PDR, where you may examine and order copies of publicly available documents, is open by appointment. To make an appointment to visit the PDR, please send an email to
PDR.Resource@nrc.gov
or call 1-800-397-4209 or 301-415-4737, between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. eastern time (ET), Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays.
B. Submitting Comments
The NRC encourages electronic comment submission through the Federal rulemaking website (
https://www.regulations.gov). Please include Docket ID NRC-2026-4588 in your comment submission.
The NRC cautions you not to include identifying or contact information that you do not want to be publicly disclosed in your comment submission. The NRC will post all comment submissions at
https://www.regulations.gov
as well as enter the comment submissions into ADAMS. The NRC does not routinely edit comment submissions to remove identifying or contact information.
If you are requesting or aggregating comments from other persons for submission to the NRC, then you should inform those persons not to include identifying or contact information that they do not want to be publicly disclosed in their comment submission. Your request should state that the NRC does not routinely edit comment submissions to remove such information before making the comment submissions available to the public or entering the comment into ADAMS.
II. Discussion
Pursuant to section 50.75 of title 10 of the
Code of Federal Regulations
(10 CFR), “Reporting and recordkeeping for decommissioning planning,” the NRC requires nuclear power reactor licensees to adjust annually, in current year dollars, their estimate of the cost to decommission their plants. The annual updates are part of the process for providing reasonable assurance that adequate funds for decommissioning will be available when needed.
Revision 21 of NUREG-1307, “Report on Waste Burial Charges: Changes in Decommissioning Waste Disposal Costs at Low-Level Waste Burial Facilities,” modifies the previous revision to this report issued in February 2025 (ADAMS Accession No. ML25037A226) and incorporates updates to the labor, energy, and waste burial escalation factors of the NRC minimum decommissioning fund formula. Due to the inclusion of disposal costs for low activity waste (a subset of low-level waste), unchanged low-level waste (LLW) burial charges at two of the nation's four LLW disposal facilities to which a majority of licensees are anticipated to dispose some portion of their LLW, and slightly to moderately higher charges at the remaining two facilities to which a small number of licensees are anticipated to dispose of their LLW, the minimum decommissioning fund formula amounts calculated by licensees, based on revised LLW burial factors presented in this report, will generally reflect minimum decommissioning fund requirements that are lower, on average, when compared to those previously reported by licensees in 2025.

AGENCY:
National Park Service, Interior.
                    SUMMARY:
In accordance with the Federal Advisory Committee Act of 1972, as amended, the National Park Service (NPS) is hereby giving notice of the 318th meeting of the Cape Cod National Seashore Advisory Commission (Commission).
                    DATES:
The Commission will meet via teleconference and in person on Monday, November 2, 2026. The meeting will begin at 1:00 p.m. and will end by 4:30 p.m. (Eastern).
                    ADDRESSES:
                        The meeting will be held in the classroom at the Salt Pond Visitors Center, 50 Nauset Road, Eastham, Massachusetts 02642. The meeting is open to the public and a virtual participation option will be available for those who are unable to attend in person. Information on joining the teleconference will be available to the public on the Cape Cod National Seashore website at least two weeks prior to the meeting at 
                        https://www.nps.gov/caco/learn/management/advisory-commission.htm.
                    
            
                SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
The Commission was established by section 8 of Public Law 87-126, as amended, and expired on September 26, 2018. The Commission was reestablished by Div. DD, title VI, subtitle B, section 613 of Public Law 117-328, the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023. The Commission's new termination date is September 26, 2029. The purpose of the Commission is to consult with the Secretary of the Interior, or his designee, with respect to matters relating to the development of Cape Cod National Seashore, and with respect to carrying out the provisions of the Act establishing the Seashore.
                    Interested persons may make oral presentations to the Commission. Such requests should be made to the Superintendent at the beginning of the meeting. Depending on the number of persons wishing to speak, and the time available, the time for individual comments may be limited. Written comments can be sent to Jennifer Flynn (see 
                    FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT
                    ). All comments received will be provided to the Commission.
                
The Commission meeting location may change based on inclement weather or exceptional circumstances. If the meeting location is changed, the Superintendent will issue a press release and use local newspapers to announce the change. Detailed minutes of the meeting will be available for public inspection within 90 days of the meeting.
                    Purpose of the Meeting:
                     The Commission will discuss the following:
                
1. Adoption of Agenda
2. Approval of Meeting Minutes from last meeting
3. Superintendent Update: Development Updates
- Planned 2026 construction activities
- Update on the Cable Road (Eastham) Multimodal Trail design and construction project
- Coastal Bluff erosion and park infrastructure: Adaptive Retreat planning
- Park projects being developed and planned for 2027 and beyond
4. Discussion on Cape Cod Character to identify defining natural, landscape and historic features to be preserved within the Seashore boundaries. Cape Cod Character is identified in the Act to establish the Seashore but not defined. Commission members will report out on what their community is protecting through local and regional policy and regulation.
Make recommendations to the Superintendent on characteristics to protect.
5. New Business: Member opportunity to identify emerging issues or future meeting agenda items.
6. Public Comment
7. Adjournment
                    Meeting Accessibility/Special Accommodations:
                     The meeting is open to the public. Please make requests in advance for sign language interpreter services, assistive listening devices, or other reasonable accommodations. We ask that you contact the person listed in the 
                    FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT
                     section of this notice at least seven (7) business days prior to the meeting to give the Department of the Interior sufficient time to process your request. All reasonable accommodation requests are managed on a case-by-case basis.

                     Before including your address, phone number, email address, or other personal identifying information in your comment, you should be aware that your entire comment—including your personal identifying information—may be made publicly available at any time. While you can ask us in your comment to withhold your personal identifying information from public review, we cannot guarantee that we will be able to do so.
                
(Authority: 5 U.S.C. Ch.10.)
                    Alma Ripps,
Chief, Office of Policy.

                    DATES:
Written comments must be received on or before November 23, 2026.

                        NMFS.Pr1Comments@noaa.gov. The request should set forth the specific reasons why a hearing on this application would be appropriate.
                    
            
                SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
                    The subject permit is requested under the authority of the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972, as amended (MMPA; 16 U.S.C. 1361 
                    et seq.) and the regulations governing the taking and importing of marine mammals (50 CFR part 216).
                
                    The applicant requests a 2-year permit to harass and film cetaceans for a documentary film about the ecological relationships between sharks and cetaceans and the anthropogenic threats they face, including opportunistic filming of sharks feeding on marine mammal carcasses. Up to 5 humpback whales (
                    Megaptera novaeangliae), 5 minke whales (
                    Balaenoptera acutorostrata), 100 common dolphin (
                    Delphinus delphis), 100 Atlantic white-sided dolphins (
                    Lagenorhynchus acutus), and 50 bottlenose dolphins (
                    Tursiops truncatus) may be harassed, observed, and filmed annually by vessel, unmanned aircraft system, and underwater divers.
                
                    In compliance with the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (42 U.S.C. 4321 
                    et seq.), an initial determination has been made that the activity proposed is categorically excluded from the requirement to prepare an environmental assessment or environmental impact statement.

                    Federal Register
                    , NMFS is forwarding copies of the application to the Marine Mammal Commission and its Committee of Scientific Advisors.
                
                    Dated: October 19, 2026.

Deputy Director, Office of Protected Resources, National Marine Fisheries Service.

The DoD (referred to herein as “the Department of War” or “DoW”) is publishing this notice to announce that the following Federal Advisory Committee meeting of the STIB will take place.

This meeting is being held under the provisions of chapter 10 of title 5 United States Code (U.S.C.) (commonly known as the “Federal Advisory Committee Act” or “FACA”), 5 U.S.C. 552b(c); and 41, Code of Federal Regulations CFR 102-3.140 and 102-3.150.
Purpose of the Meetings:
The STIB's mission is to provide independent advice and recommendations on matters supporting DoW's scientific, technological, and innovative enterprises. The objective of the meeting is to obtain, review, and evaluate classified information related to the STIB's mission. The STIB will meet with DoW Leadership to receive classified remarks regarding current and future objectives of the DoW and will meet for plenary sessions where the STIB members will have classified discussions regarding a potential Digital Solutions study and a potential Difficult Target Defeat study that may be tasked
( printed page 66694)
to the STIB, as well as having a classified discussion regarding other potential topics of study based on the remarks made by leadership during the meeting.
Agenda:
The meeting will begin at 9:00 a.m. on Wednesday, November 4th. Ms. Elizabeth Kowalski, Designated Federal Officer and Dr. Mitch Nikolich, Chair of the STIB, will provide opening remarks and a classified overview of potential topics that are likely to be tasked to the STIB for study. At 9:30 a.m., the Honorable Steve Feinberg, Deputy Secretary of War, will meet with the STIB to provide classified remarks regarding current and future objectives of the Department. Next, from 10:30 a.m. to 11 a.m., the Honorable Michael Duffy will meet with the STIB to provide classified remarks regarding modernization efforts for acquisition and sustainment. The Board will have a break from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. From 1:00 p.m. to 1:30 p.m., the Honorable Elbridge Colby will meet with the STIB to provide classified remarks regarding National Defense strategy and strategic prioritization. From 1:30 p.m. to 2:00 p.m., Mr. David Lorch will meet with the STIB to provide classified remarks regarding integrating and transitioning advanced technologies. This will be followed by a 15-minute break. From 2:15 p.m. to 4:15 p.m., the Board will meet in plenary session to hold a classified discussion regarding study topics currently under consideration by leadership to task the board and to discuss potential studies based on the remarks made by leadership during the meeting. At 4:15 p.m., Dr. Mitch Nikolich will provide closing remarks. The meeting will adjourn at 4:30 p.m.

In accordance with section 5 U.S.C. 1009(d) and 41 CFR 102-3.155, the DoW has determined that this STIB meeting will be closed to the public. Specifically, the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering, in consultation with the DoW Office of General Counsel, has determined in writing that the meeting will be closed to the public because it will consider matters covered by 5 U.S.C. 552b(c)(1). The determination is based on the consideration it is expected that discussions throughout will involve classified matters of national security concern. Such classified material is so intertwined with the unclassified material that it cannot reasonably be segregated into separate discussions without defeating the effectiveness and meaning of the overall meetings. To permit the meeting to be open to the public would preclude discussion of such matters and would greatly diminish the ultimate utility of the STIB's findings and recommendations to the Secretary of War and to the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering.
Written Statements:
In accordance with 5 U.S.C. 1009(a)(3) and 41 CFR 102-3.140, interested persons may submit a written statement for consideration by the STIB at any time. Individuals submitting a written statement should submit their statement to the STIB DFO at the email address provided above in the

Abstract:
This Information Collection Request (ICR) renewal supports activities to implement the National Oil and Hazardous Substances Pollution Contingency Plan (NCP), Subpart J (40 CFR 300.900),
Use of Dispersants and Other Chemicals and Biological Agents. The use of bioremediation agents, dispersants, surface washing agents, solidifiers, herding agents and other substances (
e.g.
sorbents) in response to oil spills in U.S. waters or adjoining shorelines is governed by Subpart J of the NCP regulation (40 CFR 300.900). Subpart J requirements include criteria for listing oil spill mitigating agents on the NCP Product Schedule and sorbent products on the Sorbent Product List. EPA's regulation, which is codified at 40 CFR 300.900, requires that EPA prepare a schedule of “dispersants,
( printed page 66700)
other chemicals, and other spill mitigating devices and substances, if any, that may be used in carrying out the NCP.” Requirements under Subpart J of the NCP are required by section 311(d)(2)(G) of the Clean Water Act (CWA), as amended by the Oil Pollution Act of 1990. The NCP Product Schedule and Sorbent Product List are used by Federal On-Scene Coordinators (FOSCs), Regional Response Teams (RRTs), and Area Planners to identify spill mitigating agents in preparation for and response to oil spills. Under Subpart J, manufacturers who want to add a product to the NCP Product Schedule or Sorbent Product List must submit technical product data including applicable toxicity and efficacy testing data to the EPA as stipulated in 40 CFR 300.915. Subpart J requires the manufacturer to submit the corresponding technical product data along with other detailed information to the EPA Office of Resource Conservation and Recovery, Office of Land and Emergency Management. The NCP Product Schedule and Sorbent Product List are available to Federal On-Scene Coordinators (FOSCs), Regional Response Teams (RRTs), and Area Committees for helping them select the most appropriate products to use in various spill scenarios.
In June 2023 EPA promulgated a final rule (88 FR 38280, June 12, 2023). This rule revised Subpart J of the NCP by adding new testing and listing criteria for products to be listed on the NCP Product Schedule and establishing the Sorbent Product List. Effective June 10, 2026, only products that are submitted and listed based on the amended testing and listing criteria will be listed on the NCP Product Schedule. AGENCY:
National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Commerce.
ACTION:
Notice; issuance of renewal incidental harassment authorization.
SUMMARY:
In accordance with the regulations implementing the Marine Mammal Protection Act (MMPA), as amended, notification is hereby given that NMFS has issued a renewal incidental harassment authorization (IHA) to Turnagain Marine Services (TMC) to incidentally harass marine mammals incidental to the Seward Cruise Ship Passenger Dock and Terminal Facility project in Seward, Alaska.
DATES:
This renewal IHA is valid from September 25, 2026, through September 20, 2027.
ADDRESSES:
Electronic copies of the original application, renewal request, and supporting documents (including NMFS
Federal Register
notices of the original proposed and final authorizations, and the previous IHA), as well as a list of the references cited in this document, may be obtained online at:
https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/permit/incidental-take-authorizations-under-marine-mammal-protection-act.
In case of problems accessing these documents, please call the contact listed below.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Carter Esch, Office of Protected Resources, NMFS, (301) 427-8401.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Background
The MMPA prohibits the “take” of marine mammals, with certain exceptions. Sections 101(a)(5)(A) and (D) of the MMPA (16 U.S.C. 1361et seq.) direct the Secretary of Commerce (as delegated to NMFS) to allow, upon request, the incidental, but not intentional, taking of small numbers of marine mammals by U.S. citizens who engage in a specified activity (other than commercial fishing) within a specified geographical region if certain findings are made and either regulations are promulgated or, if the taking is limited to harassment, an incidental harassment authorization is issued.
Authorization for incidental takings shall be granted if NMFS finds that the taking will have a negligible impact on the species or stock(s) and will not have an unmitigable adverse impact on the availability of the species or stock(s) for taking for subsistence uses (where relevant). Further, NMFS must prescribe the permissible methods of taking and other “means of effecting the least practicable adverse impact” on the affected species or stocks and their habitat, paying particular attention to rookeries, mating grounds, and areas of similar significance, and on the availability of such species or stocks for taking for certain subsistence uses (referred to here as “mitigation measures”). NMFS must also prescribe requirements pertaining to monitoring and reporting of such takings. The definition of key terms such as “take,” “harassment,” and “negligible impact” can be found in the MMPA and NMFS's implementing regulations (see 16 U.S.C. 1362; 50 CFR 216.103).
NMFS' regulations implementing the MMPA at 50 CFR 216.107(e) indicate that IHAs may be renewed for additional periods of time not to exceed 1 year for each reauthorization. In the notice of proposed IHA for the initial IHA, NMFS described the circumstances under which we would consider issuing a renewal for this activity and requested public comment on a potential renewal under those circumstances. Specifically, on a case-by-case basis, NMFS may issue a one-time 1-year renewal IHA following notice to the public providing an additional 15 days for public comments when (1) up to another year of identical, or nearly identical, activities as described in the Detailed Description of Specified Activities section of the initial IHA issuance notice is planned or (2) the activities as described in the Description of the Specified Activities and Anticipated Impacts section of the initial IHA issuance notice would not be completed by the time the initial IHA expires and a renewal would allow for completion of the activities beyond that described in the
DATES
section of the notice of issuance of the initial IHA, provided all of the following conditions are met:
A request for renewal is received no later than 60 days prior to the needed renewal IHA effective date (recognizing that the renewal IHA expiration date cannot extend beyond 1 year from expiration of the initial IHA).
The request for renewal must include the following:
An explanation that the activities to be conducted under the requested renewal IHA are identical to the activities analyzed under the initial IHA, are a subset of the activities, or include changes so minor (e.g.,
reduction in pile size) that the changes do not affect the previous analyses, mitigation and monitoring requirements, or take estimates (with the exception of reducing the type or amount of take).
A preliminary monitoring report showing the results of the required monitoring to date and an explanation showing that the monitoring results do not indicate impacts of a scale or nature not previously analyzed or authorized.
Upon review of the request for renewal, the status of the affected species or stocks, and any other pertinent information, NMFS determines that there are no more than minor changes in the activities, the mitigation and monitoring measures will remain the same and appropriate, and the findings in the initial IHA remain valid.
On September 5, 2025, NMFS issued an IHA to TMC to take marine mammals incidental to the Seward Cruise Ship Passenger Dock and Terminal Facility project in Seward, AK (90 FR 44047, September 11, 2025), effective from September 21, 2025, through September 20, 2026. As described in the application for the renewal IHA, the activities for which authorization of incidental take is requested consist of activities that are covered by the initial authorization but will not be completed prior to its expiration.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Title:
Requirements for Recognition as a VA Accredited Organization.
Type of Review:
Revision of a currently approved collection.
Abstract:
In order for an organization to provide representation to claimants before VA regarding claims for VA benefits, the organization must be recognized by VA for that purpose. Section 5902(a) of title 38, United States Code, authorizes VA to recognize organizations for the limited purpose of ensuring competent representation of veterans in claims for benefits administered by VA. VA implemented this authority in 38 CFR 14.628. An organization must apply for VA recognition, supplying information as specified in section 14.628 to demonstrate that it satisfies the legal requirements for recognition. (Organizations may provide services to veterans without VA recognition if the services do not include the preparation, presentation, and prosecution of claims for VA benefits.) The information submitted by the organizations in conjunction with a request for recognition is used by VA in reviewing accreditation applications to determine whether organizations meet the requirements for VA recognition under section 14.628. VA relies on this information to ensure that it is granting recognition only to organizations that can provide long-term, competent representation to VA claimants.
An agency may not conduct or sponsor, and a person is not required to respond to a collection of information unless it displays a currently valid OMB control number. The

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
A. Purpose
The GSA routinely hires, reassigns, promotes, or transfers Federal employees to duty stations in foreign areas (
i.e.,
outside of the United States and its territories and possessions). Civilian employees located in foreign areas are eligible for different compensation authorities compared to employees located in the United States or its territories or possessions. Besides basic pay, certain foreign allowances are often used as recruitment or retention incentives to make foreign service more attractive and economically feasible. One type of allowance is called a “living quarters allowance,” or “LQA,” and allows an agency to reimburse the cost of rental housing as well as utilities (such as electricity, natural gas, and water service). Under this authority (conveyed by the Overseas Differentials and Allowances Act of 1960, Pub. L. 86-707, Sept. 6, 1960, codified at 5 U.S.C. 5923(a)(2)), not all job candidates or overseas employees are necessarily eligible (for example, if Government-provided housing is made available). In addition, for those job candidates who are eligible, the amount of the benefit varies by rank (
i.e.,
GS grade), presence overseas with or without family, and overall family size. Detailed rules concerning eligibility and other matters are found in the State Department's
Department of State Standardized Regulations,
sections 031.12 and Chapter 130.
To more effectively administer LQA, GSA created GSA Form 5039, “Living Quarters Allowance Eligibility Questionnaire”. This form collects basic demographic and housing-related information. It also includes questions meant to coordinate housing benefits between the U.S. military and other Federal agencies (for example, if two spouses work for different Federal agencies). Individuals who complete this pre-employment questionnaire are considered job candidates and members of the public (if not already Federal civilian employees). The purpose of this data collection is to ensure that eligible applicants receive allowance consideration, in the correct amounts based on the position and family size, and that ineligible candidates are not erroneously provided with this significant monetary benefit.
B. Annual Reporting Burden
Respondents:
25.
Responses per Respondent:
1.
Total Annual Responses:
25.
Hours per Response:
2.
Total Burden Hours:
50.
C. Public Comments
A 60-day notice was published in the
Federal Register
at 91 FR 9852 on February 27, 2026. Three comments were received that contained a total of six (6) suggestions, all of which we found very helpful.
First, a commenter suggested that within the form we could briefly summarize the Department of State eligibility criteria so that users of the form would not have to independently search elsewhere. Second, a commenter suggested that we add a new section to provide definitions of three significant terms: “actual place of residence,” “personal reasons,” and “single employer test.” Third, a commenter suggested that we incorporate a document attachment checklist. A fourth comment was that we should increase the time burden estimate because of the need to locate and attach outside documents to the GSA form. The commenters also suggested that the form completion process could be automated, by developing a system to both pre-fill the demographic data and then electronically transmit the form to the agency.
We have implemented several of these suggestions by revising the form in ways to include additional information. First, we have incorporated a new section that provides easy-to-understand definitions for the three terms of art identified by the commenter. We also have incorporated a new section that summarizes, in lay language, the Department of State regulations that govern allowance eligibility. For the third comment, to add a checklist, we note that Section D of the form already includes a checklist. We believe that this existing checklist should be sufficient. For the fourth comment, regarding time burden, we agree, and have therefore doubled the estimated time to a total of 2 hours: 1 hour to complete the form and then a separate
( printed page 66707)
hour to locate and collect other supplementary documents, when they are needed. In terms of the two comments concerning automation of the completion and submission process, at GSA specifically, we do not currently have an existing information technology system that could serve this purpose. At GSA, since we currently have fewer than 25 employees annually transferred or hired for overseas work, the cost of this automation would most likely exceed the cost savings in labor hours from that automation.
We thank the commenters for their helpful feedback.
Richard Speidel,
Deputy Chief Data Officer, General Services Administration.

articles.full_text:
AGENCY:
Departmental Offices, U.S. Department of the Treasury.
                    ACTION:
Notice of information collection; request for comment.
                    SUMMARY:
The Department of the Treasury, as part of its continuing effort to reduce paperwork and respondent burden, invites the general public and other federal agencies to comment on the proposed information collection listed below, in accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995.
                    DATES:
Written comments must be received on or before December 21, 2026.
                    ADDRESSES:
                        Send comments regarding the burden estimate, or any other aspect of the information collection, including suggestions for reducing the burden, to U.S. Department of the Treasury, Attention: Treasury PRA Clearance Officer, 1500 Suite #8100, JBAB, 250 Murray Lane SW, BLDG 410/Door 123, Washington, DC 20222, or email at 
                        PRA@treasury.gov.
            
                SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
                    Title: Fraud.gov
                     Tip Intake and Referral Form.
                
                    OMB Control Number:
                     1505-0284.
                
                    Type of Review:
                     Extension without change of a currently approved collection.
                
                    Description:
                     The Department of the Treasury is launching a government-wide intake and referral portal for members of the public to report suspected waste, fraud, abuse, improper payments, misuse of Federal funds, and related misconduct affecting Federal programs at 
                    Fraud.gov. The collection supports Treasury's implementation of Executive Order 14249, “Protecting America's Bank Account Against Fraud, Waste, and Abuse,” and Executive Order 14395, “Establishing the Task Force To Eliminate Fraud.” On behalf of the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, Treasury will collect information necessary to receive, review, triage, categorize, de-duplicate, and refer allegations to the appropriate Federal agency, inspector general, law enforcement organization, or other authorized entity for review and potential action. The collection also supports program integrity, payment integrity, oversight, fraud prevention, and related administrative functions. The tip intake form hosted on 
                    Fraud.gov
                     allows respondents to provide a narrative description of their allegations, supporting documentation, contact information and related information necessary to evaluate and route submissions. An artificial intelligence tool will process the initial entry and populate it into standardized fields, along with suggested routing recommendations, which respondents can review and edit before submitting. The tool is intended to assist with standardization and routing recommendations; respondents may review and edit populated fields before submission, and Treasury personnel will apply appropriate review and quality-control procedures before referral.
                
                    Form: Fraud.gov
                     Tip Intake and Referral Form.
                
                    Affected Public:
                     Individuals and Households.
                
                    Estimated Number of Respondents:
                     80,000.
                
                    Frequency of Response:
                     Once.
                
                    Estimated Total Number of Annual Responses:
                     80,000.
                
                    Estimated Time per Response:
                     30 minutes.
                
                    Estimated Total Annual Burden Hours:
                     40,000.
                
                    Request for Comments:
                     Comments submitted in response to this notice will be summarized and included in the request for Office of Management and Budget approval. All comments will become a matter of public record. Comments are invited on: (a) whether the collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the agency, including whether the information shall have practical utility; (b) the accuracy of the agency's estimate of the burden of the collection of information; (c) ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; (d) ways to minimize the burden of the collection of information on respondents, including through the use of technology; and (e) estimates of capital or start-up costs and costs of operation, maintenance, and purchase of services required to provide information.
                
                        (Authority: 44 U.S.C. 3501 
                        et seq.)
                    
                    Spencer W. Clark,
Treasury PRA Clearance Officer.

October 19, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),[1]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,[2]
notice is hereby given that on October 9, 2026, Cboe Exchange, Inc. (“Exchange” or “Cboe Options”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Cboe Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “Cboe Options”) proposes to amend (i) Rule 5.33(g) to allow a complex order consisting of legs in different groups of series in the class to Leg into the Simple Book, in addition to being posted to the
( printed page 66745)
Complex Order Book (“COB”), where the Exchange has designated those groups as a related group and (ii) Rule 5.34 to allow for the Exchange (and Users, when applicable) to set risk control parameters on a related group basis when the Exchange is permitted to set parameters on a group basis. The text of the proposed rule change is provided in Exhibit 5.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 5.33, which governs the trading of complex orders. The proposed additions to Rule 5.33(g)(6) would establish a related group framework under which a complex order consisting of legs in different groups of series in the class may Leg into the Simple Book, in addition to being posted to the COB, if the Exchange has designated those groups as a related group and the other applicable legging restrictions that are currently enumerated under Rule 5.33 are satisfied.
Additionally, the Exchange also proposes to add interpretative guidance under Rule 5.34 to establish that, when the Exchange sets parameters for risk controls on a group basis, that the Exchange (or Users, when applicable) may also set parameters for a related group.
Background
Currently, the Exchange has authority under Rule 4.13(f) to list SPX or VIX on a group basis.[3]
The Exchange currently lists SPX on a group basis; specifically, the Exchange lists A.M.-settled SPX options under the symbol SPX and lists P.M.-settled SPX options under the symbol SPXW. While SPX and SPXW options are part of the same S&P 500 Index options class, the Exchange may apply different trading parameters to SPXW options than those it applies to SPX options (pursuant to Rule 1.5).[4]
SPX options reside on one matching engine while SPXW is on a separate matching engine. The Exchange intends to launch Weekly A.M.-settled SPX options (“SPXO”) [5]
and list SPXO options as a separate group from both SPX and SPXW. However, SPXO and SPX options will both be on the same matching engine.
Legging
Under Rule 5.33(g) (“Legging”), a complex order may execute against orders and quotes resting in the Simple Book (pursuant to subparagraphs (d)(5)(A) and (e)) if it can execute in full or in a permissible ratio and has no more than the maximum number of legs, as the Exchange determines on a class-by-class basis, and is subject to a list of restrictions. Specifically, one such restriction under Rule 5.33(g)(6) states that “[i]f the Exchange determines to list SPX or VIX on a group basis pursuant to Rule 4.13, a complex order consisting of legs in different groups of series in the class may not Leg into the Simple Book. A complex order consisting of legs in the same group of series may Leg, subject to the other restrictions in this paragraph (g).” Pursuant to this provision, a complex order that consists of SPX and SPXW option legs is currently unable to leg into each underlying leg's Simple Book. The primary reason for this provision is because the Simple Books for SPX and SPXW are on different matching engines, as noted above.
However, SPXO options will be on the same matching engine as SPX options. As a result, Exchange technology will allow complex orders comprised of legs from these two different groups (SPXO and SPX) to leg into their respective Simple Books.[6]
Complex orders that include an SPX or SPXO leg and an SPXW leg will continue to not be able to leg into their respective Simple Books.
In order to account for this, the Exchange proposes to add the related group framework to Rule 5.33(g)(6) so that a complex order consisting of legs in different groups of series in the class that Cboe has designated as related groups may Leg into the Simple Book, in addition to being posted to the COB. The proposed related group framework reflects the current technological limitations of the Exchange's system. The Exchange will announce groups designated as related groups via Exchange Notice. The proposed change does not alter the existing Legging restrictions in Rule 5.33(g); rather, it adds a framework under proposed paragraph (g)(6) for the Exchange to designate groups as related, and thus permit complex orders comprised of legs from different groups to leg into their respective Simple Books, if Exchange technology can accommodate legging of complex orders comprised of legs for different groups. Because the Exchange remains unable to leg complex orders comprised of legs for groups that reside on different matching engines, only groups whose relevant series are processed by the same matching engine may be eligible for designation as a related group.

October 19, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”),[1]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,[2]
notice is hereby given that on October 5, 2026, Long-Term Stock Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “LTSE”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Exchange filed the proposal as a “non-controversial” proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act [3]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.[4]
The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange is filing with the Commission a proposed rule change to adopt Supplementary Material .02 to Rule 14.210 (Dually-Listed Securities) to specify that all companies listing securities on LTSE must be listed on another registered national securities exchange (“Supplementary Material .02”).
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The self-regulatory organization has prepared summaries, set forth in Sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to adopt Supplementary Material .02 to Rule 14.210 (Dually-Listed Securities) to specify that all companies listing securities on LTSE must be listed on another registered national securities exchange (“Supplementary Material .02”).
While LTSE maintains primary listing standards in its Rulebook and intends to operate as a primary listing market in the future, LTSE currently lists only issuers that also maintain a primary listing on another national securities exchange. The proposed rule text does not modify or eliminate LTSE's underlying initial or continued listing standards; instead, it clarifies the relationship between those standards and LTSE's current listing model for dually listed issuers.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the provisions of Section 6 of the Act,[5]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,[6]
in particular, in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest.
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change promotes just and equitable principles of trade and protects investors by providing clear and transparent rules regarding LTSE's current listing model. Although LTSE maintains comprehensive primary listing standards within its Rulebook, LTSE currently operates under a model where listed issuers maintain a dual listing on another registered national securities exchange. The Exchange believes that codifying this requirement in proposed Supplementary Material .02 ensures that issuers, investors, and market participants have clarity regarding the requisite dual-listing status for LTSE-listed securities. By eliminating potential ambiguity surrounding LTSE's current listing operations, the proposed rule change prevents confusion in the marketplace and ensures that all market participants operate with a shared, precise understanding of LTSE's dual-listing framework.
Importantly, the proposed rule text does not modify, relax, or eliminate LTSE's existing initial or continued listing standards.[7]
Instead, it simply clarifies the practical application of those standards in relation to LTSE's present operating model. By preserving underlying quality and governance benchmarks while harmonizing rule text
( printed page 66757)
with operational reality, the Exchange maintains high listing standards that promote market integrity without disrupting existing trading mechanisms or regulatory oversight across the national market system.
The mandatory dual-listing requirement under Supplementary Material .02 will apply uniformly to all issuers listing securities on LTSE. Furthermore, the proposed rule change is identical in substance to existing rules previously approved or adopted by other self-regulatory organizations. Specifically, the proposed rule text mirrors Nasdaq Texas, LLC (“Nasdaq TX”) IM-5220-1, which similarly requires all companies listing on that exchange to maintain a dual-listing on another national securities exchange.[8]
Adopting an identical approach establishes regulatory consistency across listing venues.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule change fosters intermarket competition by clarifying the parameters under which issuers may list on LTSE while maintaining their primary listings elsewhere. Because the rule is substantively identical to Nasdaq Texas IM-5220-1, it ensures a level playing field among national securities exchanges that operate dual-listing structures.
The proposed rule will apply equally to all issuers listing securities on LTSE. Because the proposed rule merely codifies current operational practice and explicitly preserves the Exchange's underlying listing standards, it imposes no unexpected burdens on issuers or market participants while fostering fair and open competition within the national market system.
